title: Best De'Longhi Dehumidifier (2026): Models, Recalls & Manuals
dek: One allergy certification no rival can match, two recalls worth understanding — here's how to shop De'Longhi's lineup with confidence.
description: The best De'Longhi dehumidifier for 2026, from the compact DEX16F to the AAFA-certified DDX45E and 50-pint pump model, plus recall checks and manual tips.
intro: Most Americans know De'Longhi for espresso machines and space heaters, but the De'Longhi dehumidifier lineup has a distinction few brands can claim: its 45-pint DDX45E and pump-equipped DDX45PE carry the **asthma & allergy friendly** certification, a program run with the Asthma and Allergy Foundation of America (AAFA).

There's a second thing worth knowing before you buy. De'Longhi's name has appeared in two separate fire-hazard recalls, from two unrelated contract manufacturers, in 2013 and 2021. Neither affects units on store shelves today, but one of them uses the exact same model names De'Longhi still sells — which matters a lot if you're buying used.
Below are the four current De'Longhi models worth considering, how to tell a recalled unit from a safe one, and where to find your manual.
topPicksLead: For most rooms, the **De'Longhi DDX45E** is the one to buy: an AAFA-certified 45-pint unit for spaces up to about 500 square feet.

products.name: De'Longhi 45-Pint Dehumidifier (DDX45E)
pros: Carries the asthma & allergy friendly certification
cons: Rated for rooms up to about 500 sq ft
products.whyWeLoveIt: If allergies or asthma are why you're shopping, the DDX45E offers something no competitor does: independent certification that it holds a target humidity range and keeps allergen exposure low during routine filter and tank maintenance.
products.performance: De'Longhi rates it at 45 pints a day for spaces up to about 500 square feet — think bedroom, living room or a single finished basement room rather than an open basement. It drains to a tank or through a continuous-drain hose. Owners tend to praise the straightforward controls. For the full breakdown of the certification, see our [dehumidifier for allergies](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-allergies/) guide.

products.name: De'Longhi 45-Pint Dehumidifier with Pump (DDX45PE)
pros: Pump pushes water up to 16 feet
Same allergy certification as the DDX45E
Drains to a sink or window, no bucket
cons: Name matches a 2021 recall listing — check used units
products.whyWeLoveIt: It's the DDX45E with a built-in pump. If your drain isn't downhill from where the unit sits, the pump moves water up and out so you never have to haul a tank.
products.performance: De'Longhi lists the same 45-pint rating and room coverage as the DDX45E, plus a pump that can lift condensate up to 16 feet overhead. The pump is the only functional difference, so choose it only if you need it. Because a pre-2017 DDX45PE appears in the 2021 New Widetech recall, verify the manufacture date on any secondhand unit. See all self-draining options in our [dehumidifiers with a pump](/best/best-dehumidifier-with-pump/) guide.

products.name: De'Longhi 50-Pint ENERGY STAR Dehumidifier with Pump
pros: Rated for up to 4,500 sq ft
cons: Not part of the allergy-certified pair
products.whyWeLoveIt: For anything bigger than a single room, this is the De'Longhi to buy. It's the brand's largest current U.S. consumer model, and it pairs 50-pint capacity with a pump so basement placement isn't limited by drain location.
products.performance: De'Longhi rates it for up to 4,500 square feet and lists a carbon filter, LCD controls, an adjustable humidistat, a 24-hour timer and auto-defrost. It's part of De'Longhi's newer ENERGY STAR generation. Retailers sometimes discount this capacity tier during promotions, so it's worth comparing a few sellers. See how it compares with other big units in our [basement dehumidifier](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-basement/) picks.

products.name: De'Longhi 15-Pint Dehumidifier (DEX16F)
pros: Small enough for a bedroom or closet
products.whyWeLoveIt: Not every damp spot calls for a 45-pint machine. The DEX16F is De'Longhi's entry point, sized for a bedroom, walk-in closet or small home office.
products.performance: It's rated at about 15 pints a day and is sold with built-in air filtration. Drainage is by tank or a gravity hose on a level surface. Expect it to cycle on and off in a small, closed room rather than run flat out. For more one-room options, see our [best small dehumidifier](/best/best-small-dehumidifier/) picks.

items.label: Separate CPSC recalls naming De'Longhi dehumidifiers (2013 and 2021)
Dehumidifier line with the asthma & allergy friendly certification

blocks.text: Since 2005, De'Longhi has also co-owned a joint-venture factory with TCL in Zhongshan, China, that builds dehumidifiers and portable air conditioners for both brands — more on that in our [best TCL dehumidifier](/best/best-tcl-dehumidifier/) guide.

We don't lab-test. We compare De'Longhi's published capacity and coverage ratings, ENERGY STAR listings, manuals and certification records, then read owner reviews for recurring problems. Because of the brand's history, we also cross-checked every current model name against CPSC recall notices.
We ranked on how well each model fits a real room, then drainage, health certification and value.

sections.heading: What to look for in a De'Longhi dehumidifier

items.label: Room size, not just pints
items.text: The 45-pint pair is rated for about 500 square feet. Anything larger calls for the 50-pint model.

items.label: Pump only if you need it
items.text: The DDX45PE matches the DDX45E in every way except the pump.

items.label: Allergy certification
items.text: If asthma or allergies drive your purchase, the DDX45E and DDX45PE are the only certified dehumidifiers.

items.label: Buy new, or check the date
items.text: New retail stock postdates both recalls. For used units, check the manufacture date or serial number first.

items.label: A plan for upkeep
items.text: Clean the filter every few weeks in heavy use; our [maintenance guide](/guides/dehumidifier-maintenance/) covers the rest.

sections.heading: De'Longhi dehumidifier recalls: what to check

blocks.text: In September 2013, the CPSC announced a recall of roughly 2.2 million dehumidifiers sold under 12 brand names, all made by Gree Electric, over overheating and fire risk. De'Longhi's DDSE30 and DDSE40 were among the named models.

In 2021, a separate manufacturer, New Widetech, recalled about 2 million dehumidifiers sold under several brand names from 2009 through August 2017. The De'Longhi models listed include DD30P, DD40P, DD45, DD45E (certain serial ranges), DD45P, DD45PE, DD50P, DD50PC, DD50PE, DD50PSC, DD50PSCE, DD70PE, **DDX45PE, DDX50PE and DDX70PE**.

blocks.title: Same name, different generation
blocks.text: The recall covers only units made before September 1, 2017. Today's DDX45PE is a later generation and isn't affected — but the model name is identical, so the label alone won't tell you which you have. On a secondhand unit, check the manufacture date or serial number against the recall lookup before plugging it in.

The model number and serial number are on a rating label on the back or side of the cabinet. Enter the model on De'Longhi's U.S. support site to download the instruction manual and operating instructions. The manual is where you'll find the error-code list, filter-cleaning steps and how to set up continuous drainage or the pump hose.

items: **Won't collect water?** Check the room temperature and humidistat setting first; see our [not collecting water](/guides/dehumidifier-not-collecting-water/) guide.
**Icing on the coils?** The room may be too cold; our [freezing up](/guides/dehumidifier-freezing-up/) guide explains why.
**Unsure of the setting?** Start at 45–50% and adjust; our [humidistat settings guide](/guides/dehumidifier-humidistat-settings-guide/) has seasonal targets.

blocks.text: If a De'Longhi has reached the end of its life — or turns out to be a recalled unit — don't just leave it at the curb. Our [how to dispose of a dehumidifier](/guides/how-to-dispose-of-a-dehumidifier/) guide explains refrigerant-safe recycling options.

The **De'Longhi DDX45E** is the best De'Longhi dehumidifier for most rooms, with a health certification no competitor matches. Choose the **DDX45PE** if you need a pump, the **50-pint ENERGY STAR model** for a basement, and the **DEX16F** for a bedroom or closet. New stock isn't touched by either recall, but check the manufacture date on any secondhand De'Longhi. See how the brand ranks against the field in our [best dehumidifier brands](/best/best-dehumidifier-brands/) roundup.

faqs.q: What is the best De'Longhi dehumidifier?
faqs.a: For most rooms, the DDX45E, an allergy-certified 45-pint unit rated for spaces up to about 500 square feet. Choose the DDX45PE for a built-in pump, the 50-pint ENERGY STAR pump model for a basement, or the DEX16F for a bedroom or closet.

Yes, twice, by two different manufacturers. Gree-built DDSE30 and DDSE40 models were part of a 2013 recall, and a long list of New Widetech-built models made before September 1, 2017, were recalled in 2021. Both involved fire risk.

faqs.q: Is the De'Longhi DDX45PE sold today the recalled model?
faqs.a: No. The 2021 recall covers DDX45PE units made before September 1, 2017. Current units are a later generation, but they share the same name, so check the manufacture date or serial number on any used unit.

faqs.q: Where can I find a De'Longhi dehumidifier manual?
faqs.a: Find the model number on the rating label on the back or side of the unit, then search it on De'Longhi's U.S. support site to download the instruction manual and operating instructions.
It varies by model and era. De'Longhi co-owns a joint-venture factory with TCL in Zhongshan, China, while the recalled units were built by outside contract manufacturers Gree and New Widetech.

faqs.q: What does the asthma & allergy friendly certification mean?
faqs.a: It means the DDX45E and DDX45PE passed independent testing showing they hold a target humidity range and limit allergen exposure during routine filter and tank maintenance.

faqs.q: How do I clean a De'Longhi dehumidifier filter?
faqs.a: Unplug the unit, slide out the filter from behind the front or rear grille, rinse it under lukewarm water, let it dry completely and reinstall it. Every two to three weeks in heavy use is a good rhythm; check your manual for the exact location.
